nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: There is a box speaker above the fire door. It used to carry the school bell. It is still switched on.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: A whole class is talking on the other side of the wall. The voices run together, then stop all at once, as if someone has just come in.

nodes.speaker: q
nodes.text: That is C's lot. They do that.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The speaker clicks twice and goes quiet.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: A cleaning trolley is parked across the cupboard, wheels turned in.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: A mop, half a bucket of water, and a bottle of yellow cleaning fluid. The cupboard behind them seems to be full of exercise books; you can make out the spines.

nodes.speaker: q
nodes.text: Leave the bucket. It has been there since Monday.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You leave the trolley alone. It blocks the cupboard, but there is room to get past it.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You stop by the railing. The yard looks different from up here than it did through the classroom window. Even the colours seem to have changed.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Two hoops, a shed, a stretch of concrete. You watch for a while. Nothing much happens.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The lesson carries on without you. You don't mind as much as you thought you might.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: You stood at the walkway railing during the free period and watched the yard.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You stop at the railing again. The yard below, the two hoops, the shed - all where you left them.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: Don't look at the yard. Look at the piece of railing the wall is behind.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: The teaching block is what blocks the western light. At this hour the railing should lay seven or eight upright shadows across this wall, evenly spaced.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: There is nothing on the wall. A railing is a railing and a wall is a wall, and the thin black layer that should sit between them has been taken away.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: Outside it was a wall with no shadow. This is inside. Two places, two directions, two kinds of light. This is no longer a matter of how I see it.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You put your hand between the railing and the wall. The wall takes no shadow of your hand either. The walkway is still bright. The dust is still dust.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You draw your hand back and wipe it on your trousers.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: When something has a wall behind it, it casts nothing; it casts nothing, and it is still there.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You come back to the railing. The yard below is the yard: two hoops, a shed.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You do not turn around to look at the wall behind you.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: I could look for you.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: No.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: So you lean on the railing and watch the yard. You can work out where the light is and where the shadows should fall. You just don't.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: You stood at the walkway railing again during the free period and watched the yard.
